messages:
Oncall Bot: INCIDENT ALERT — gcp asia-northeast1 egress instability affecting Private Connect customers. Symptoms: intermittent BGP withdrawals, increased packet loss on customer-facing prefixes. Ticket INC-2031456789. Paging infra-oncall.

Maya R: paging infra-oncall, seeing alerts in console.

Lucas (SRE): oncall here. I can see loss and BGP neighbor flaps for our partner peer 169.254.100.3. Control plane otherwise healthy. Bringing up netops.

Ash N - NetOps: I have the peer session resets in the gateway logs. Sample:

```
Apr 04 04:22:12 gateway01 bgpd[1234]: %BGP-5-ADJCHANGE: neighbor 169.254.100.3 Down - BGP neighbor reset
Apr 04 04:22:42 gateway01 bgpd[1234]: %BGP-5-ADJCHANGE: neighbor 169.254.100.3 Up - BGP neighbor established
Apr 04 04:23:10 gateway01 kernel: rx dropped pkts=1200 if=eth2
```

Ash N - NetOps: drops correlate with flaps, looks like metro fabric congestion on partner side (POP-A <-> POP-B).

Lucas (SRE): are only Private Connect customers impacted or public egress too?

Priya (Customer Success - Priya): Customer reports are all for private endpoints (on-prem via interconnect). Several customers seeing 502/timeout spikes.

Derek H: can we fail traffic to the tokyo backup egress? We have cross-region fallback routes for these prefixes.

Ash N - NetOps: Yes, we have a GRE backup to tokyo2 with established BGP. Primary path wins today due to higher local-pref. We can temporarily lower local-pref on the primary or raise local-pref on backup. Prefer a controlled change: set backup local-pref +200 for affected prefixes.

Lucas (SRE): plan: 1) Change route selection to prefer tokyo backup for impacted prefixes, 2) monitor for 10m, 3) open case with partner/GCP, 4) keep CS notified. Need Maya approval to proceed.

Maya R: approve. Proceed with temporary pref change and keep it bounded (<=60m) unless partner confirms fix. Notify customers after cutover.

Ash N - NetOps: performing change now. Command (cloud router/partner config):

```bash
# adjust advertised priority on our cloud router peer to prefer backup path
gcloud compute routers update-bgp-peer \\
  --router=redwood-asia-router \\
  --peer-name=partner-asia-1 \\
  --advertised-route-priority=250  # lower priority so backup path chosen
```

Ash N - NetOps: applied change at 04:37 UTC. Watching BGP and egress metrics.

Lucas (SRE): seeing BGP session stable to backup and graceful shift of traffic. Packet loss dropped from ~6% to <0.5% for affected prefixes. Rolling averages look good.

Oncall Bot: Auto-update: Impact RED -> YELLOW (partial degradation). Pager suppression engaged.

Priya (Customer Success - Priya): Notifying impacted customers with templated message: "We've rerouted your traffic to a backup egress due to partner metro congestion. We're monitoring and will update when primary is healthy."

Derek H: opened a support case with GCP partner and provider: CASE-GP-98765. Partner acknowledges transient metro congestion and working a repair. ETA 45-60m.

Ash N - NetOps: provider responded: they see queueing between POP-A and POP-B and are flushing hardware buffer/migrating flows.

Lucas (SRE): continuing to monitor. I'll keep the pref change for 60 minutes then test reverting to primary. If partner still unstable, we'll extend and schedule post-incident follow-up.

Maya R: capture all commands and timeline for postmortem. Also mark any customers who requested a credit/incident report.

Lucas (SRE): adding timeline to the incident doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/INC-2031456789 (placeholder). I'll hand off to morning shift at 07:00 UTC.

Ash N - NetOps: final status from provider at 05:20 UTC: fabric repair completed, BGP flaps stopped, no further packet drops observed. Reverted pref at 05:38 UTC and validated primary path stable.

Lucas (SRE): confirmed revert and baseline metrics normal. Closing active mitigation. Monitoring for 2 hours.

Maya R: thanks all. We'll run a short postmortem focusing on detection threshold and automated failover playbook gaps.

Oncall Bot: INCIDENT INC-2031456789 status: MITIGATED -> MONITORING. Handoff: infra-oncall -> day-sre. Tags: #incidents #postmortem :thumbsup:
